topic: The Physics of Pi: Colliding Blocks and Numerical Discovery
target_audience: Undergraduate physics or computer science students

sections.title: Introduction: The Unexpected Appearance of Pi
lecture_lines: Can colliding blocks calculate digits of Pi?
Consider two blocks sliding on a frictionless surface.
The mass ratio determines the collision dynamics.

sections.title: Prerequisite Physics: Conservation Laws
lecture_lines: Elastic collisions conserve both momentum and energy.
Momentum is the product of mass and velocity.
Kinetic energy remains constant during these perfect bounces.
animations: Show momentum conservation equation in blue #0000FF.
Show kinetic energy conservation in green #00FF00.

sections.title: The Mechanism: Mapping Collisions to Angles
lecture_lines: Phase space represents the state of our blocks.
Collisions trace a circular arc in this space.
Each bounce represents a specific angle of rotation.

Show angle change after each collision in #FF00FF.

sections.title: The Pi Connection: Geometric Interpretation
lecture_lines: Large mass ratios create a full semicircle path.
Total collisions reveal digits of Pi.
Geometric arc length maps perfectly to Pi.
animations: Display title 'Geometric Interpretation of Pi' in #FFFFFF.

sections.title: Conclusion and Real-World Application
lecture_lines: Physical interactions can compute transcendental numbers.
Pi emerges from simple collision rules.
